titulo: Today I have eaten, yesterday I ate
intro: Two ways to talk about the past. Time words help you choose, although usage changes by region.
p.esta mañana.consejo: This morning is still part of today. That is why «esta mañana he desayunado» sounds natural in Spain.
p.esta semana.consejo: The current week includes today. In Spain it usually takes the perfecto: «esta semana he trabajado mucho».
p.este año.consejo: A year that has not ended is still open. You say «este año he viajado poco».
p.alguna vez.consejo: It is used to ask about experiences: «¿Has comido paella alguna vez?». It is written as two words.
p.nunca.consejo: With the perfecto it goes before the verb: «nunca he ido». You do not need to add «no».
p.ayer.consejo: It is a finished day. That is why it takes the indefinido: «ayer comí pizza». The y sounds as in «yo».
p.anoche.consejo: It is one word: «anoche». It talks about a finished moment, so you say «anoche cené».
p.el lunes pasado.consejo: It works with any day: «el martes pasado». It is a finished time, so use the indefinido.
p.la semana pasada.consejo: «Pasada» agrees with «semana»: feminine. With «el año pasado» it is «pasado», masculine.
p.el año pasado.consejo: A year that has already closed. «Año» is written with ñ, which sounds «ny»: «el año pasado fui a Perú».
p.hace un año.consejo: «Hace» + time counts back from today: «hace dos meses». The h is silent and the c sounds «th».
p.el otro día.consejo: It does not say which day, but it is a finished past: «el otro día vi a Marta».
p.he ido.glosa: I have gone, I have been
p.he ido.consejo: «Ir» has the participle «ido». With «nunca»: «nunca he ido a Perú».
p.fui.consejo: «Fui» is also the indefinido of «ser». Context tells you which one: «fui al cine».
b1.texto:
To choose between two pasts, look at the time word.

If the time **includes the present**, in Spain the **perfecto** is used:

- **Esta mañana he comido** fruta.
- **Esta semana he viajado** poco.
- **Este año** no **he visto** a mi tía.
- ¿**Has estado** alguna vez en Perú? **Nunca he ido.**

If the time **has ended**, the **indefinido** is used:

- **Ayer comí** a las cuatro.
- **Anoche cené** tarde.
- **El lunes pasado fui** al médico.
- **El año pasado**, **hace un año** or **el otro día**.

It is a useful guide for Spain, not a law: in many parts of America the indefinido is also used with «hoy» or «esta semana». You will hear both forms.
b2.f0.texto: Have you ever been to Peru?
b2.f2.texto: I have never been to Peru.
b2.f3.texto: This year I have travelled very little.
b2.f5.texto: This morning I have had a coffee.
b2.f6.texto: Last night I had dinner very late.
b2.f7.texto: Yesterday I had lunch at four.
b4.texto:
One question solves almost everything: **has that time ended?**

- **Not ended** (esta mañana, esta semana, este año, alguna vez, nunca): **perfecto**. **He ido, hemos comido.**
- **Ended** (ayer, anoche, el lunes pasado, la semana pasada, el año pasado, hace un año): **indefinido**. **Fui, comimos.**

With **alguna vez** and **nunca** you ask about or talk about an experience without giving a date: **¿Has ido alguna vez?** **Nunca he ido.** As soon as you give a closed date, you switch: **Fui el año pasado.**

Remember: in many parts of America the indefinido is also used with open times. Both options are understood everywhere.
b4.e0.texto: This week I have read two books.
b4.e1.texto: Last Monday we went to the cinema.
b4.e2.texto: A year ago I bought this house.
b5.f0.texto: This morning I have opened the window of my room.
b5.f1.texto: The fresh air has brought a sweet smell of warm bread.
b5.f2.texto: A pink light has touched the roofs of the square.
b5.f3.texto: This year I have lived many quiet mornings like this one.
b5.f4.texto: I have not yet heard a single voice in the street.
b5.f5.texto: Last night it rained on the roofs for hours.
b5.f6.texto: Yesterday I ate a hot soup in a small bar.
b5.f7.texto: Last Monday I saw an enormous rainbow over the river.
b5.f8.texto: Last year I travelled at night on a silent train.
b5.f9.texto: A year ago I bought a small house by the sea.
b6.o0.refuerzo: That's it! Last night is over: it asks for the indefinido.
b6.o1.refuerzo: This week includes today: it is still open.
b6.o2.refuerzo: It gives no date: it talks about life up to now.
b6.pregunta: Which word marks a finished time?
b7.o0.refuerzo: Well done: this morning is still within today, and in Spain it asks for the perfecto.
b7.o1.refuerzo: It is future: the morning in the sentence has already happened.
b7.o2.refuerzo: It is for nosotros, and the sentence is about yo.
b8.frase: El año pasado fui a Perú
b8.traduccion: Last year I went to Peru
b9.o0.refuerzo: «Ayer» is a closed day: the indefinido goes here.
b9.o1.refuerzo: Correct: «nunca» looks at all of life up to now.
b9.o2: El año pasado fui a Perú
b9.o2.refuerzo: Last year is over: it is a closed event.
b9.pregunta: Which sentence talks about life up to today?
b10.o0.refuerzo: Well done! Last week is over: indefinido.
b10.o1.refuerzo: The perfecto needs a time that is still open, and that week has ended.
b10.o2.refuerzo: «Voy» is present and the sentence is about the past.
b10.pregunta: Which form of ir completes the sentence?
b12.o0.refuerzo: Yes: «¿Has estado alguna vez en Perú?» asks for no date.
b12.o1.refuerzo: It gives a closed date: it asks for the indefinido.
b12.o2.refuerzo: It counts back from today: it is a specific moment.
b12.pregunta: Which expression asks about an undated experience?
p.cené.consejo: The accent marks the past: «ceno» is now, «cené» is yesterday.
p.leído.consejo: The accent splits the vowels: «le-í-do», not «leido».
p.rosada.consejo: It ends in -a because it describes the feminine noun «luz».
p.tocado.consejo: The c before a sounds like k: «tocado».
p.bar.consejo: It is written like the English word, with a clear final r.
p.arcoíris.consejo: The accent on í splits the vowels: «ar-co-í-ris».
